rationale: This study is a cluster-randomised controlled trial (experimental design) across 332 rural villages (121 clusters) in the Democratic Republic of Congo evaluating the national Healthy Villages and Schools (Villages et Ecoles Assainis, VEA) programme. Among the review's legal/institutional mechanism families, the central rule-type mechanism tested is participation_assistance: the 9-step VEA protocol mandates collective community adoption and action planning, election and training of a village WASH committee, NGO/Health Zone facilitation and assistance, and achievement of seven norms (including a dynamic village WASH committee) for formal certification. Outcomes span multiple co-central families: preregistered primary outcomes measure effective_access (time spent collecting water, quantity of water collected, and use of an improved drinking water source) alongside primary_connection/coverage of improved water and sanitation infrastructure, while secondary outcomes prominently evaluate administrative_outcome (village water governance index, which increased by 1.3 SDs) and economic_access (financial cost of water index). Thus primary_outcome_family is effective_access and assigned_outcome_label_with_multiple is multiple.
